newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Aktas to raise '97 sales at inflation rate.
newsitem.headline: Turk Aktas to raise '97 sales at inflation rate.

text.p: Turkish private electricity distributer Aktas Elektrik Ticaret A.S. aims to raise turnover by at least the rate of inflation in 1997 compared with turnover of 20 trillion lira expected in 1996, a senior company official said.
The Turkish government sees inflation running at 65 percent in 1997, according to its draft budget estimate.

"We do not expect government subsidies in energy any more. Therefore, we expect energy prices to rise by at least the inflation rate in 1997. In that case, our turnover will increase as much as the inflation rate," Turan Aydemir, general manager of the company told Reuters.
He said the profitability of Aktas was mainly affected by unlicensed electricity usage and transmisison breakdowns.

The rate of unlicensed usage and transmission loss accounted for 16.5 percent of the power distributed by Aktas in 1995 and the company aims to reduce it by some four percent by 1997 through a 1.02 trillion lira investment programme.
"If approved by the Energy Ministry, we want to more than double our investment spending next year," Aydemir said.
Aktas shares traded at 105,00 lira in afternoon trade on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, against Wednesday's 107,500 close.
The gross profit margin of Aktas has risen sharply since it posted a 5.81 trillion lira turnover and a 110.4 billion lira loss in 1994.
